findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct move 2's 'same contract it always had' claim to scope preservation to signing only, and state an explicit decision about the non-claimable fast-fail: either forward --force so the bare verb still reviews any ticket (matching old behavior) or document the exit-0→2 / no-LLM divergence as intended and reflect it in the happy-path/edge ACs.
evidence: Plan move 2: 'A caller who scripted `rebar review <id>` therefore gets the same "read-only opinion, nothing written" contract it always had'

`_review_plan` docstring (src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py:441-443): 'A ticket that is not yet claimable (status closed/idea/blocked, or open but blocked by an unclosed dependency) fast-fails to INDETERMINATE with no LLM unless --force is passed. Exit ... 2 on INDETERMINATE.'
Old `_review` body (lines 191-206) calls `llm.review_ticket(...)` unconditionally — no claimability gate — and returns 0/1.

The --help AC (AC line for test_help_states_the_behaviour_differences) DOES list 'fast-fails with no LLM on a non-claimable ticket' as a disclosed difference, so this is a supersession the plan acknowledges elsewhere but the move-2 wording contradicts.
findings.finding: Move 2 claims the shim preserves 'the same read-only opinion... contract it always had', but review-plan fast-fails to INDETERMINATE (exit 2), running no LLM, on a non-claimable ticket unless --force is passed — so `rebar review <non-claimable-id>` changes from 'runs the LLM, returns findings, exit 0/1' to 'exit 2, no LLM'. The shim suppresses signing (--no-sign) but makes no decision about --force, so this exit-code/behavioral divergence is unhandled at the forwarding layer.
findings.location: Approach → 'The six moves', move 2 ('keeps its read-only semantics'); Scope → src/rebar/_cli/_llm_commands.py
scenarios: A CI script runs `rebar review <id>` where the ticket is still an idea or is blocked by an open dependency; today it prints review findings and exits 0, after the change it exits 2 with no LLM output
An operator eyeballs a closed ticket with `rebar review <id>` for a second opinion — previously worked, now fast-fails
findings.suggested_fix: In move 2, narrow the preservation claim to 'preserves the unsigned/no-write contract' and add a sentence: since review-plan fast-fails (exit 2, no LLM) on a non-claimable ticket while old `rebar review` reviewed any status, decide whether the shim also forwards --force (restoring review-any-ticket) or intentionally adopts the fast-fail — and add an AC asserting the chosen exit code for a non-claimable ticket.
